messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: Dedicated reserved GPU pool 'resv-usw2-7' is at 100% capacity (region us-west-2). Affected tenants: VelvetPay (enterprise-resv-72) experiencing >3m queue growth and 429 throttles. Autoscaler attempting but failing to provision new nodes.

maria: oncall (pager) here, looking. Seeing the same — queues for VelvetPay up ~12k requests, avg queue time 18s, thundering of long-running batched jobs.

tim: digging into autoscaler logs, two failures:
```
ERROR autoscaler: provision failed: quotaExceeded: Requested GPUs exceed account quota
attempts=3 region=us-west-2 pool=resv-usw2-7
```
also seeing 'scale_attempt_limit_reached' for pool.

ajay: quick question — is this noisy neighbor or legitimate traffic spike from VelvetPay?

maria: initial traces show VelvetPay is hot — a scheduled batch job misconfigured sending huge concurrency. But other tenants also get throttled. Noisy neighbor + pool already at cap.

elaine: checking reservations: resv-usw2-7 is 100% pinned to enterprise reservations: VelvetPay (60%), GeminiRetail (25%), smaller tenants (15%). No free capacity.

maria: mitigation options:
1) apply short-term per-tenant throttle for VelvetPay to reduce queue (risky for SLA)
2) migrate some less-critical reservations to other regions / pools (time-consuming)
3) request cloud quota increase (takes hours)
4) route VelvetPay to hosted fallback model in hosted fleet (we can do immediate but violates dedicated SLA)

alex-cs: VelvetPay is a paying enterprise with hard SLI. They will escalate if we route off-dedicated. Need ETA and notification text.

maria: proposing immediate step: 1) throttle VelvetPay to 50% concurrency for 10m, 2) open cloud quota request, 3) prepare hosted fallback as last resort. Need SRE + infra signoff.

ajay: +1 to throttle. Also start eviction plan for any long-running non-prod jobs in the pool. Can you identify candidates?

tim: listing long-running containers now... found 3 GPU jobs tagged 'dev' owned by 'gemini-retail-internal'. Can evict with minimal impact.

maria: evicting dev jobs now (dry-run -> then kill):
```
# list
kubectl get pods -n dedicated --selector=pool=resv-usw2-7,env=dev -o wide
# evict
kubectl delete pod <podname> --grace-period=30
```

maria: evicted 3 dev pods, freed 0.5 GPUs. Not enough.

deploy-bot: autoscale attempt 4 -> failed (quotaExceeded)

maria: applying per-tenant throttle rule now (ratelimit config):
```
PATCH /routing/policies/resv-usw2-7
{ "tenant_overrides": { "velvetpay": { "concurrency_limit": 5, "burst": 10 } } }
```

maria: throttle applied. Observing queue drop for VelvetPay from 12k -> 4.5k in 6 minutes. Avg queue time down to 6s.

alex-cs: notifying VelvetPay account: "We’re seeing elevated request volume affecting your dedicated capacity. We’ve applied a temporary concurrency cap to protect service stability and are working on capacity increase. ETA ~2h for quota response. We’ll update within 30m." Want me to send?

maria: yes please send. Include workaround: reduce batch concurrency and retry with exponential backoff.

alex-cs: sent. Customer replied: "Please escalate — this is production traffic. We're seeing increased latency in payments." They requested priority.

ajay: I'm taking ownership for escalation to infra. Opening ticket with cloud provider to raise GPU quota (+8 GPUs) and setting priority. Ticket #CLOUD-7891.

tim: two more mitigations: 1) enable emergency burst pool: we have 'dedicated-burst' with spare nodes in other region (us-west-1) — would need cross-region networking and customer consent. 2) as last resort, route VelvetPay to hosted fleet with same model version and IP allowlist.

maria: status check at +30m: queue for VelvetPay 3.2k, overall queue across pool 5.6k. Throttles down but customers still impacted. Cloud ticket is P1.

ajay: cloud provider responded: provisional quota increase approved for 4 GPUs within 45m, full review may take longer. They requested justification and billing confirmation.

maria: applying incremental actions: 1) accept 4 GPU temp quota, 2) prepare hosted fallback plan in case ticket stalls.

maria: accepted 4 GPUs; autoscaler retried and successfully provisioned +4 GPUs to resv-usw2-7. Pool capacity up 20%.

deploy-bot: nodes added -> 4 g4dn.xlarge

maria: queue stabilized. VelvetPay queue now 700 requests, avg wait 1.2s. Rolling back throttle partially to concurrency 10.

alex-cs: VelvetPay acknowledges and thanks for quick action but requests RCA and compensation. I've scheduled a call with their SRE for 30m.

ajay: handing off to SRE lead for follow-up & postmortem. Actions for follow-up:
- root cause: customer batch misconfig + insufficient autoscaler headroom
- short-term: improve alerting thresholds for per-tenant queue growth
- medium-term: policy: reserve emergency burst GPUs and automated cross-pool spillover
- long-term: rate-limits on scheduled bulk jobs and per-tenant backpressure guidance

maria: handing pager to ajay for follow-up. Oncall clear for now. :white_check_mark:

ajay: got it. I'll drive the postmortem and coordinate CS & infra. Assigning owners and timeline in the postmortem doc.

maria: thanks all. Closing incident thread after postmortem triage.
